topicName: Delta Lake Integration and ACID Transactions
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Delta Lake Integration and ACID Transactions in Apache Spark"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covers how to integrate Delta Lake with Apache Spark to ensure ACID transactions, scalable metadata handling, and time travel capabilities over your data lake storage."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Spark Session Configuration"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To use Delta Lake with Apache Spark, you need to configure your SparkSession to include the Delta Spark package and extension. Below is the standard way to initialize a SparkSession with Delta support enabled."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("DeltaLakeTutorial") \
    .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension") \
    .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog") \
    .getOrCreate()"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Writing Data to Delta Format"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Writing DataFrame results to a Delta table is identical to writing to Parquet, except you specify 'delta' as the format. This creates the transaction log (_delta_log) alongside your data files."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"data = [(1, "Alice", 100), (2, "Bob", 200), (3, "Charlie", 300)]
columns = ["id", "name", "salary"]

df = spark.createDataFrame(data, columns)

# Write as Delta table
df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/tmp/delta-table")"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Enforcing ACID Transactions with Upserts (MERGE)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"One of the primary benefits of Delta Lake is support for ACID transactions, enabling complex operations like MERGE (upsert) safely on cloud object storage without risk of partial writes or dirty reads."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from delta.tables import DeltaTable

# Load the Delta table
deltaTable = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, "/tmp/delta-table")

# New updates or incoming data
newData = [(2, "Bob Updated", 250), (4, "David", 400)]
newDf = spark.createDataFrame(newData, columns)

# Perform MERGE (Upsert)
deltaTable.alias("oldData").merge(
    newDf.alias("newData"),
    "oldData.id = newData.id"
).whenMatchedUpdate(set={
    "name": "newData.name",
    "salary": "newData.salary"
}).whenNotMatchedInsert(values={
    "id": "newData.id",
    "name": "newData.name",
    "salary": "newData.salary"
}).execute()"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Time Travel and Auditing"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Delta Lake maintains a history of all transactions. You can query older versions of data using timestamp or version number parameters, which is critical for auditing and rollback scenarios."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# Read the table as of version 0 (before the merge operation)
old_df = spark.read.format("delta").option("versionAsOf", 0).load("/tmp/delta-table")
old_df.show()

# View transaction history
deltaTable.history().show(truncate=False)"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ACID Transactions: All modifications to the Delta table are atomic, consistent, isolated, and durable."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scalable Metadata: Delta Lake handles petabyte-scale tables with billions of files easily using Spark metadata."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Time Travel: Easily revert or query previous iterations of your datasets."}]
